message.content:
Here are calcium-containing foods organized by category, based on the search results:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Dried skimmed milk powder (100g) | 1,590 mg |
| Yogurt, plain low-fat (8 oz/1 cup) | 415–448 mg |
| Milk, skim/nonfat (1 cup) | 299–325 mg |
| Milk, whole (1 cup) | 276–300 mg |
| Mozzarella, part-skim (1.5 oz) | 333 mg |
| Cheddar cheese (1.5 oz) | 306 mg |
| Ricotta, part-skim (1/2 cup) | 337 mg |
| Cottage cheese, 1% fat (1 cup) | 138–276 mg |

## Fortified Plant-Based Foods

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Almond milk, fortified (1 cup) | 482 mg |
| Soy milk, fortified (1 cup) | 299–399 mg |
| Orange juice, calcium fortified (1 cup) | 349 mg |
| Rice milk, fortified (1 cup) | 300 mg |
| Breakfast cereals, fortified (1 serving) | 100–1,000 mg |
| Fortified instant cereals (100g) | up to 1,333 mg |

## Fish (with bones)

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Sardines, canned in oil with bones (3 oz) | 324–325 mg |
| Sardines in tomato sauce (100g) | 430 mg |
| Sardines in oil (100g) | 500 mg |
| Salmon, pink canned with bones (3 oz) | 181 mg |

## Soy Products & Legumes

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Tofu, firm made with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 204–253 mg |
| Tofu, firm (1/4 block) | 553 mg |
| Tofu, steamed (100g) | 510 mg |
| Tofu, soft made with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 138 mg |
| Edamame, cooked (1 cup) | 130 mg |
| Soybeans, cooked (1/2 cup) | 131 mg |

## Dark Green Leafy Vegetables

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Collard greens, cooked (1 cup) | 268–324 mg |
| Kale, cooked (1 cup) | 94–177 mg |
| Kale, raw (1 cup) | 24–90 mg |
| Bok choy (Chinese cabbage), cooked (1 cup) | 74–158 mg |
| Turnip greens, boiled (1/2 cup) | 99 mg |
| Broccoli, cooked (1 cup) | 62–76 mg |
| Broccoli, raw (1/2 cup) | 21–35 mg |
| Okra, stir fried (100g) | 220 mg |
| Watercress (100g) | 170 mg |
| Spring greens, boiled (100g) | 75 mg |

**Note:** Spinach contains calcium but has very low absorption (only ~5%) due to high oxalic acid content.

## Nuts & Seeds

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Sesame seeds (100g) | 670 mg |
| Chia seeds (1 oz) | 179 mg |
| Chia seeds (1 tbsp) | 76 mg |
| Almonds (1 oz/30g) | 75–76 mg |
| Sesame paste (tahini) (1 tbsp) | 64 mg |
| Brazil nuts (1 oz) | 45 mg |

## Fruits

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| Dried figs (4) | 54 mg |
| Dried apricots (100g) | 73–250 mg |
| Orange (1 medium) | 47–65 mg |
| Blackberries (1 cup) | 42 mg |

## Other Foods

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| White bread (100g) | 177 mg |
| Whole wheat bread (1 slice) | 30 mg |
| Flour tortilla (10-inch) | 90 mg |
| Corn tortilla (6-inch) | 46 mg |
| Baked beans (1/2 cup) | 53–60 mg |
| Whey protein (100g) | 485 mg |

## Key Points About Calcium Absorption:
- **Dairy products and fortified foods:** ~30% absorption rate
- **Certain plant foods** (broccoli, kale, bok choy): Similar absorption to milk when low in oxalic acid
- **Spinach:** Only ~5% absorption due to high oxalic acid
- **Vitamin D** is essential for proper calcium absorption

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.webmd.com/food-recipes/guide/calcium-vitamin-d-foods
4. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
5. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
6. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
7. https://imsear.searo.who.int/bitstreams/99ce16a3-83a5-4fba-8f33-d0c9a0428303/download
8. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
9. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_834FM.pdf?uid=598797444&uid2=2020111220184122
